```{r,echo=FALSE}
# sqrt(x/a) = b


b = sample(2:5,1)
a = sample(c(2:5,10),1)*sample(c(-1,1),1)
x = a*b^2

eq = paste0("\\sqrt{\\frac{x}{",a,"}}=",b)
eq2 = paste0("\\frac{x}{",a,"}=",b^2)

eq3 = paste0("\\sqrt{\\frac{",x,"}{",a,"}}\\stackrel{?}{=}",b)
eq4 = paste0("\\sqrt{",round(x/a),"}\\stackrel{?}{=}",b)

```

Question
========

Solve.

$$`r eq`$$

Solution
========

Square both sides.

$$`r eq2`$$

Multiply both sides by `r a`.

$$x=`r x`$$

Check the solution in the original equation.

$$`r eq3`$$

$$`r eq4`$$

Yup, that is true. So $x=`r x`$ is a solution to the given equation.
